memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The Lord said to Moses: "Make two trumpets of hammered silver, and use them for calling the community together and for having the camps set out. When both are sounded, the whole community is to assemble before you at the entrance to the tent of meeting." - Num 10:1-3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God instructed Moses to make two silver trumpets. Their purpose was to gather the people and to signal when it was time to move. When the trumpets sounded, the whole community knew to assemble before the Lord at the tent of meeting. It was God's way of calling His people together.

There is something comforting in this. God did not leave His people to wander in confusion, each person guessing what to do. He gave a clear call — a sound everyone could recognise — that drew them together and gave them direction. When the trumpet blew, they knew to come.

God still calls His people to gather. We are not meant to live our faith in isolation, each drifting along alone. The New Testament urges us not to give up "meeting together" but to keep gathering to encourage one another (Heb 10:25). There is strength, comfort, and direction when God's people come together in His presence.

The trumpets also remind us of a greater gathering still to come. Scripture tells us that one day a trumpet will sound and God will gather His people to Himself forever (1 Thess 4:16). The call that once summoned Israel to the tent of meeting points ahead to the day Christ gathers His own.

When you hear God's call to gather with His people, respond gladly. And live in hope of that final trumpet, when we shall all be gathered home.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you value gathering with God's people, or drift toward isolation?
- How does meeting together strengthen and encourage you?
- How does the hope of that final "trumpet" shape your life?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You call Your people together. Help me not to isolate myself, but to gladly gather with others in Your presence. Amen.
